title: An early DM fit for FRB20190117A lowers mean squared error by 64 percent on six later Catalog 2 days
abstract: We test time trends in dispersion measure for 11 known repeating fast radio burst sources in CHIME/FRB Catalog 2, release 20251231. An early fit for FRB20190117A lowers mean squared error from 5.359 to 1.952 on six later days, a reduction of 63.6 percent. Only three later days improve. A paired resample interval for prediction skill includes zero. The full-data slope is +1.010 pc cm^-3 yr^-1 and stays positive in the tested spectral and burst-shape checks. Published high resolution values already show the rise. No new source or confirmed plasma change is reported. A fixed-ionization expanding shell alone has the wrong derivative sign if the measured rise is physical. Measurement bias, correlated days, and a small validation sample limit the result. No independent telescope confirmation of the DM trend was found. Code, retained inputs, hashes, full source tests, figures, and reproduction steps are included.
